shortDescription: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures closed down on Wednesday after setting a four-week low on expectations that Black Sea export disruptions may ease, analysts said.

children: Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures closed down on Wednesday after setting a four-week low on expectations that Black Sea export disruptions may ease, analysts said.

Ukraine and Russia have both voiced an interest in a limited ceasefire involving grain and energy-related targets, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said after meeting Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov in New York.
Cargo movements in the Black Sea region are at a near standstill due to heavy attacks on ships and port infrastructure by both sides.
As a result, top wheat importers in Asia, the Middle East and Africa that count on the Black Sea region for grain have been finding it hard to secure supplies.
Continued attacks on ports and vessels tempered expectations of a recovery in grain shipments.
Technical selling added pressure on prices, traders said.
CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) closed down 8-3/4 cents at $7.08-1/2 per bushel.
K.C. December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) was last down 9-1/2 cents at $7.71-3/4 a bushel, while Minneapolis December spring wheat (MWEZ26) was down 9 cents at $7.28-3/4 a bushel.
